title: Data Zoning Gateway with per-customer exemptions and deterministic fallback
creator: Priya Nair
description: Implement a Data Zoning Gateway (DZG) middleware that enforces residency constraints and handles per-customer exemptions (allowlist/denylist) while providing deterministic, observable fallbacks. The gateway sits at the policy enforcement layer before routing decisions are materialized and must: (1) evaluate residency and regional constraints for each request, (2) consult tenant-scoped exemption rules and precedence, (3) select an ordered set of routing candidates (regional endpoint, model variant, proxy), and (4) apply a deterministic fallback algorithm when the preferred region is unavailable. The feature must emit detailed audit events for compliance and support a simple JSON config schema for customer-level rules.
acceptance_criteria: DZG evaluates residency rules and enforces EU-only and region-scoped routing for 100% of flagged tenants in staging
Tenant-level exemptions (allowlist/denylist) are honored with clear precedence rules and admin-level override logging

When primary region endpoints are unreachable, DZG falls back deterministically to: (a) compatible model variant in allowed region, then (b) regional proxy with data governance masking, with no silent cross-border egress for EU-only tenants
Audit trail contains request id, tenant id, evaluated policy set, decision reason, and routing target for every routed request
Routing decisions exposed to Console routing trace UI and a new compliance dashboard with counts of fallback events by tenant and reason
Automated unit and integration tests cover policy precedence, exemption handshake, and fallback ordering with mocked endpoints
technical_notes: Position: DZG will be implemented as a middleware in the routing service before kernel selection and autoscaling hooks
Policy evaluation: use the existing PDP service; add a small local cache with 10s TTL for tenant rules to avoid PDP hot loops
Deterministic fallback: stable hashing on request-id+tenant-id to pick among equivalent fallback candidates to ensure sticky behavior across retries
Compatibility checks: each fallback candidate must pass a capability filter (data residency flag, model quantization level, SLA tier) before being considered
Telemetry: emit structured events to observability pipeline with fields {request_id, tenant_id, policy_snapshot_version, decision, fallback_reason, target_region, target_model_variant}
Config schema v1: {tenant_exemptions: [{tenant_id, type: allow|deny, scope: region|egress, reason, created_by}], residency_policy: {default_region, strict_eu_only: bool, allowed_regions: []}}
Performance budget: decision latency must add <6ms p95 on 99% of requests; local cache and fast path required
Security: all exemption mutations require RBAC + audit log entry; mark ticket for security review (see security_review_required=true)
rollout_plan: 1) Merge behind feature flag. 2) Internal canary (routing team) traffic for 48h. 3) Enable for 3 pilot tenants with explicit consent and sample audit retention. 4) Gradual ramp to 25% of geo-sensitive tenants, monitor compliance dashboard and latency. 5) Full enablement for tenants with residency flags after 2 weeks of stability. Rollback plan: flip feature flag and run passive traffic dry-run to validate stateful caches are safe.
qa_steps: Create test tenant with residency_profile=EU_ONLY and verify routing never leaves EU region under normal conditions
Add tenant exemption allowlist entry and confirm requests route to configured external region and that audit entry contains override metadata
Simulate primary region outage; assert deterministic fallback selects consistent model variant across retries and that console shows fallback reason
Run load test to validate decision latency remains <6ms p95 and no error budget burn
Verify RBAC prevents unauthorized exemption edits and that each edit writes to audit log with actor and timestamp
